AccountSettings.description: A user's settings, stored on their account (ADR-027) and synced to every device. Versioned like every BT document (ADR-022): a write applies only if its `version` is newer than the stored one, so a stale device can't undo a newer change. Each control adds its field with its reader (collapse and Hide Scores S68, Video Player S70).

collapseNonFavorites.description: Fold games without a favorite team into slim bars (S68).

favoriteTeamIds.description: MLB team ids (`MLB_TEAMS`), in the order the user picked them.

hideScores.description: Hide every score and record (S68). Read it through `shouldHideScores`, never directly (owner, 2026-10-21), so the setting can outgrow an on/off switch.

videoPlayer.description: Where videos play (S70): a dialog over the page, or a stage in the Videos room.

ApiErrorResponse.description: The one error-body shape every 4xx path returns.

nextAllowedAt.description: On a 429 download refusal: the ISO time the next download may be requested (`nextDownloadAllowedAt`).

challenge.description: The challenge made during the at-bat (S95); absent when there was none, and on older recordings.

awayScore.description: The score after the play (S41), or null where MLB didn't say.

AtBatChallenge.description: A call challenged during the at-bat (S95; the live feed's `reviewDetails`, on the play or on one of its events): who challenged it, whether it was overturned, and the challenged pitch's `playId` when the review sits on a pitch (null when it sits on the play as a whole).

AtBatMetrics.description: What one at-bat meant, by MLB's own measure (S93; the play-metrics feed): the chance each team wins after it (percent, 0–100), how much it moved that chance, and MLB's flags. Keyed by the live feed's `atBatIndex`, so it joins `GameSnapshot.plays`.

hitData.description: Statcast contact on the at-bat's ball in play; each figure null when nothing was measured.

homeWinProbabilityAdded.description: Percentage points the at-bat added to the home team's chance (negative when it took some away).

leadChange.description: The at-bat tied the game or changed the lead.

BoxscoreBatter.description: One batter's line in the box score (S2; the ratified Box frames' columns).

avg.description: Season batting average after this game, as MLB formats it (`.279`).

battingOrder.description: MLB's batting-order code: `100`–`900` for starters, `101`… for whoever replaced them.

position.description: Fielding position abbreviation as MLB gives it (`CF`, `DH`, `P`).

BoxscoreInfoLine.description: One `label: value` line of MLB's boxscore notes (Venue, Weather, Att…).

DayDigestResponse.description: "Best of <date>" (S71): the day's top clips across its games, ranked by `dayDigest`.

items.description: Best first; empty on a day with no videos yet.

DigestClipGame.description: The game a digest clip comes from, enough for the player's "Go to game: NYY @ BOS, Sep 21" link.

DigestItem.description: One clip in the day digest: its place, whether to watch it first, the clip and its game.

watchFirst.description: Only the top clip (the frames' `WATCH FIRST`).

GameBoxscore.description: The box score (S2): each team's batters in batting order, and MLB's game info lines.

GameDecisions.description: The pitchers of record of a finished game (S65; W / L / S).

GameLive.description: The live moment of a game in progress (S63; the game-rooms Live frames' diamond and pitcher / batter cards): the player id on each base (`null` when empty), the batter and the pitcher. MLB's `linescore.offense` and `currentPlay.matchup`.

GamePlayMetrics.description: A game's play metrics (S93): every at-bat MLB measured, in game order.

GameRecap.description: MLB's editorial recap as plain text (S10): the headline and the article's paragraphs, separated by blank lines. Markup, embedded players and links are stripped at ingest, so views never render outside HTML.

boxscore.description: The box score (S2); absent until MLB has one, and on older recordings.

lastChangedAt.description: ISO time the content last changed — not the last poll, which is `fetchedAt`.

live.description: Who is on base and who is batting and pitching (S63); `null` unless in progress, absent on older recordings.

playMetrics.description: MLB's per-at-bat win probability and key-moment flags (S93). Absent when the feed (an internal mlb.com source) failed or had nothing: the game is served as before.

recap.description: MLB's editorial recap (S10); absent until MLB publishes one.

relatedArticles.description: mlb.com stories about the game (S94); absent, like `videoPlayRefs`, when the source failed or had none.

version.description: ADR-022: monotonic per game; bumps only when the content changes (`stampVersion`).

videoPlayRefs.description: The pitch each video shows, where MLB links one (S94). Absent when MLB's GraphQL game content (a persisted query MLB may retire) failed or had no links: the game is served as before.

HighlightKind.description: What a video is, from MLB's content keywords (S69): a play `highlight`, the game `recap`, the `condensed` game, or another `video` (interviews, lineups, analysis).

LinescoreInning.description: One inning of the linescore (S2). A side that hasn't batted in it yet — the home half of an unfinished inning, or a bottom 9th never played — has `runs: null`.

innings.description: One entry per inning played or under way, in order (S2). Absent on older recordings.

scheduledInnings.description: Innings the game is scheduled for (9 unless shortened); absent on older recordings (S2).

MeDeleteRequest.description: The body of an account deletion: the phrase the user typed, which must equal  {@link  ACCOUNT_DELETION_PHRASE }  exactly. Deleting needs no download first (owner, 2026-10-27: "Deleting and downloading aren't connected").

MeDeleteResponse.description: A finished deletion. The session that asked no longer resolves to an account.

MeDownloadFileResponse.description: A download's file: every registered personal data store's export at the time it was made.

expiresAt.description: ISO time the download stops being fetchable (14 days after it was made; `downloadExpiresAt`).

stores.description: Store name (ADR-028's inventory **Where**) → that store's export; null when it held nothing.

MeDownloadResponse.description: A stored data download (ADR-028, owner 2026-10-27): its id and when it ages out. Requesting one answers with this, never the data; the file itself is fetched by its id, signed in, while it lasts.

expiresAt.description: ISO time the download stops being fetchable (14 days after it was made; `downloadExpiresAt`).

MeResponse.description: The signed-in account, for Settings' "Signed in as {email}" (standings-search-settings A3) and for gating UI by entitlement. A projection of `UserProfile`, not the whole record: Patreon IDs and timestamps stay server-side.

email.description: Every account has an email (owner, 2026-10-28: "It should be impossible for an account to have no email."; S82).

date.description: S69: when MLB published it (ISO instant); absent on older recordings.

kind.description: S69: what the video is; absent on older recordings.

playId.description: The pitch the video shows (S95): MLB's link, or a matched ABS challenge (`playLink`); null when it shows no single play.

playLink.description: How `playId` was found (S95): MLB linked it (`guid` / `playIdRef`), or BT matched an ABS challenge clip to its challenge.

tags.description: S69: MLB's taxonomy tags (`data-visualization`, `home-run`, …); absent on older recordings.

teamIds.description: S69: the MLB team ids it features (`team_id` keywords); absent on older recordings.

breakHorizontal.description: Horizontal movement in inches, MLB's sign (S63); `null` when MLB sent none.

breakVertical.description: Vertical movement in inches including gravity, MLB's sign (S63); `null` when MLB sent none.

PlayerRef.description: A player named on the scoreboard (pitchers of record).

ProbablePitcher.description: A probable pitcher with his season line (S65; the module's "W-L, ERA"); nulls when MLB sent none.

RelatedArticle.description: An mlb.com story about the game (S94; GraphQL `relatedArticles`). MLB gives the article's slug, not a URL; whoever shows it builds the mlb.com link from the slug.

Role.description: What a user may administer. Lives in BT, not the identity provider (ADR-019: no provider RBAC).

lastChangedAt.description: ISO time the content last changed — not the last poll, which is `fetchedAt`.

version.description: ADR-022: monotonic per day; bumps only when the content changes (`stampVersion`).

decisions.description: After the game: the pitchers of record (S65); `null` until MLB names them.

live.description: During the game: runners, matchup and count (S65); `null` unless in progress.

probablePitchers.description: Before the game: who is expected to start (S65).

startTime.description: First pitch as an ISO instant (S65); views show it in the viewer's zone (`formatGameTime`).

ScheduleLive.description: The live moment on the scoreboard (S65): S63's runners and matchup, plus the count, and who is batting and pitching by name for the count slot's "AB / P" lines (S67).

ScheduleTeam.description: A team on the scoreboard (S65): the team, and its record when MLB sent one.

ScoreboardDefaultDateResponse.description: The day the scoreboard opens on (S111): today in season, the last final in the off-season.

SettingsRequest.description: A settings write: the whole document with a bumped `version`; an older version is ignored (ADR-022). `gameRowSlot` (S67), `collapseNonFavorites` and `hideScores` (S68), `videoPlayer` (S70) may be left out — each reads as its default — so a page loaded before they shipped can still save.

collapseNonFavorites.description: Fold games without a favorite team into slim bars (S68).

favoriteTeamIds.description: MLB team ids (`MLB_TEAMS`), in the order the user picked them.

hideScores.description: Hide every score and record (S68). Read it through `shouldHideScores`, never directly (owner, 2026-10-21), so the setting can outgrow an on/off switch.

videoPlayer.description: Where videos play (S70): a dialog over the page, or a stage in the Videos room.

SettingsResponse.description: The signed-in user's settings document (ADR-027); the house defaults until they first save.

SignInConfigResponse.description: How this deployment signs fans in (S116; ADR-019): its Logto tenant's address and the web app's ID, read from the Worker's `vars` (`LOGTO_ENDPOINT`, `LOGTO_APP_ID`) so the web app keeps no second copy. `logto` is null where the Worker offers no Logto sign-in: local dev (which signs in as `dev:`), previews, and staging until its own tenant exists.

appId.description: The single-page app's ID, the ID token's audience.

SignInRequest.description: A sign-in hand-off: the ID token Logto's hosted sign-in gave the web app, sent once.

SignInResponse.description: A finished sign-in: BT's own session token, which the web app sends as `Authorization: Bearer`.

StandingsPhaseName.description: Which table a standings payload is (S128): the day's regular-season standings, a season's final regular-season table (after the regular season until the next spring), or spring training's standings as of the day.

StandingsResponse.description: The division standings for one day (S4, S128): MLB's tables projected to BT's shape — the regular season's as of that day, the season's final table after it ends, spring training's in the spring (see `phase`).

date.description: The day the table stands as of; for a `final` table, its season's `regularSeasonEndDate`.

phase.description: Which table this is (S128); absent on snapshots read before S128 (recorded fixtures).

season.description: MLB's season id of the table (S128): the year it was played.

StandingsTeamRecord.description:
One team's row in a standings table.

MLB reports games-back and the elimination figures as strings, using `"-"` for "not applicable". The mapper normalizes that sentinel to `null` so the UI never has to special-case a dash.

TeamRecord.description: A team's season record (S65; the scoreboard module's `81-62`).

VideoPlayRef.description: The pitch a video shows, by MLB's own link (S94; GraphQL `playIdRef`): `videoId` is the video's id in the content feed (`MediaHighlight.id`), `playId` the pitch's `PitchEvent.playId`. It covers clips the content feed links to no play, such as ABS challenges.
